title: Linked-list walk idioms
description: The three boilerplate walks every LL problem uses: single walk, parallel walk, and dummy-head builder.

notes: Single walk: while(curr) terminates safely on null — no need to test curr.next.
Parallel walk uses && so the loop stops the moment either list runs out; attach the remainder afterwards.
Dummy head is a sentinel — it eliminates the 'is this the first node?' branch and lets you always do tail.next = ....
Always advance tail = tail.next after attaching, or you'll overwrite the same slot next iteration.

questions.q: Which loop condition safely walks a single linked list to the end?
questions.explain: while(curr) terminates cleanly when curr becomes null; while(curr.next) would skip the last node and throw if head is null.

questions.q: What does a dummy-head sentinel buy you when building a new list?
options: Removes the special case for inserting the first node
Makes the walk O(1) instead of O(n)
Lets you skip the null check
questions.explain: With a sentinel you can always do tail.next = newNode without branching on 'is this the very first append?'.

questions.q: When do you reach for the parallel walk `while (a && b)`?
options: Reversing a single list in place
Comparing or merging two lists in lockstep
Detecting a cycle in one list
questions.explain: Parallel walk is for two-list problems — merge, compare, intersection — where you advance both pointers each iteration.

questions.q: After building a list with a dummy head, what do you return?
questions.explain: dummy is the sentinel; the real list starts at dummy.next.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the single-walk loop that counts nodes in a list.
Fill in the dummy-head builder that copies values from an array into a new list.
Fill in the parallel walk that returns true only if every paired value is equal (stops the moment either list runs out).

blanks.hint: loop only while BOTH are non-null

L3.prompt: Write `doubleList(head)` that returns a NEW list with each value doubled, using the dummy-head builder. Log `JSON.stringify(toArr(doubleList(toList([1, 2, 3]))))`.
hints: Combine single walk (curr = curr.next) with the dummy-head builder.
Attach a brand-new node each step; return dummy.next, not dummy.
